title: The Tide That Learned to Speak to Stone

features.name: the listening stones
features.desc-on-touch: Arranged in rows like an orchard, each one worn smooth by tide, each one holding the shape of a question the water asked. You can feel the conversation in the polish.

features.name: the tide-mark memory
features.desc-on-touch: A stain where salt learned to speak. The line where water stopped and stone kept listening. It rises and falls each day, but today it's frozen here as a record.

features.name: the echo pool
features.desc-on-touch: Where the tide pools gather between stones. You hear yourself speaking and the stone answers, but the stone's answer comes a moment late, still learning the language.

features.name: the stone-tide dialogue
features.desc-on-touch: A recording of the conversation, tide-voice layered with stone's slow response, each turn building on the last. The stone is beginning to predict what the tide will say next.

inscription: the stones learned to answer the tide by listening to their own shape; the tide learned to speak by remembering what silence sounds like

file.name: TideStone_Dialogue_Transcripts.mp3
file.note: A recording that grew longer each night. The stone's replies came slower at first. Now they answer before the wave arrives.

reverie.title: REVERIE — tide-song at the turning hour
narr: You both stand in the shallows. The tide is speaking,
neither question nor answer, just stone and water
learning each other's names. She points: Listen. The stone
is responding. You feel it in the cold, the slow voice of rock
beginning. By tomorrow it will answer faster. By winter, it will know.
